name: Côte d'Ivoire
regionLevel: first-level division (ISO 3166-2), as in the N-Ways regions table

existing.system: No national postcode in practical use. La Poste de Côte d'Ivoire delivers to P.O. boxes written 'office code + B.P. + number + locality + office code', e.g. '06 B.P. 37 Abidjan 06' or '17 B.P. 105 Abidjan 17' (UPU sheet; home delivery codes '1xx' were only tested). La Poste also sells a 'Boîte Postale Digitale' with a postal address card and promotes what3words on its website.
existing.status: Abidjan street addressing (Projet d'adressage du District d'Abidjan, PADA, Ministry of Construction, Housing and Urban Planning) has named and signposted most streets: 12,000 of 14,279 roads (plus 35 boulevards and 211 avenues) by May 2025, with blue/white metric building numbers painted by the State (BNETD) and street-name plates; the first address certificates were issued in Koumassi/Marcory on 16 Dec 2021; completion was announced for 31 Dec 2025 (not confirmed). An address is described as 'street + number + postal code', and the project director said an international-standard postal code was introduced, but no format, lookup site, API or open data was found. Other cities are to follow.
existing.openData: No open national address register found. OSM street names (ODbL) are the only reusable source; PADA street names not confirmed as imported into OSM.
existing.openAlgorithm: Open Location Code (Plus Codes) is an open, free algorithm (Apache-2.0) and works offline; what3words (promoted by La Poste CI) is proprietary and licensed.
existing.terms: what3words requires a licence for commercial use; Plus Codes have no licence fee. No PADA data licence published.
existing.recommendation: Superseded by the issued model (docs/model.md, engine/SPEC.md): official addresses (PADA, later PAVI) first; every compound has an N-Ways code, a plate name and a 4- or 5-digit number; Plus Codes for any point. No dependence on what3words or on a postcode (none in use).
